comments.author: gregmac
comments.story_title: New speed camera ‘detect’ vehicles braking as they approach
comments.why_zh: 深刻改变了评论者对限速和道路设计的看法
comments.quote_zh: 它深刻影响了我对这些事的看法。
comments.text_zh: 我想我第一次接触这个，是来自 Not Just Bikes 一个关于限速的视频 [1]，它深刻影响了我对这些事的看法。我现在认为很多道路设计完全是坏掉的，包括限速、那个频道（以及其他相关频道）所说的“stroads”，还有交叉口（环岛 vs 红绿灯）。那个视频尤其和测速摄像头这件事高度相关。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: I think my first intro to this was from a Not Just Bikes video on speed limits [1], and that profoundly affected my opinion on this stuff. I now think a lot of road design is just utterly broken, and it includes speed limits, what that channel (and other related) refer to as "stroads", and intersections (roundabouts vs traffic lights). That video in particular is highly relevant to the speed camera thing. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: noirdujour
comments.story_title: America’s roads and highways have a big, fat style guide
comments.why_zh: 让评论者看清了规则与实际驾驶行为之间的关系
comments.quote_zh: 它真的让我看清了规则与实际行为之间的关系。
comments.text_zh: > MUTCD 设计街道的方式类似于乡村公路，这会创造出一种条件：人们在本该慢速行驶的地方却超速，因为街道的设计并不反映标志牌上要求你行驶的速度。Not Just Bikes 在一期关于限速的视频里讲到了这个短板[1]，它真的让我看清了规则与实际行为之间的关系。基本上，限速标志对驾驶速度的影响很轻微，但街道设计很重要。宽阔、开阔、笔直的道路会自然而然地促使司机开到高速公路的速度，即使在更偏郊区的区域也是如此。我经常会看一眼速度表，发现自己跟着车流开时远远超过了标示的限速，这太惊人了。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: > MUTCD designs streets similarly to rural highways, and this can create conditions where people speed when they need to be driving slowly, because the design of the street doesn't reflect the speed the sign says you need to be driving. Not Just Bikes covers this shortfall in a video on speed limits[1], and it really opened my eyes on the relationship between rules and actual behavior. Essentially, speed limit signs affect driving speeds slightly, but the street design is important. Wide, open, straight roads naturally prompt drivers to drive to highway speeds, even in more suburb areas. It's amazing how often I check the speedometer and find that I'm driving much more than the posted speed limit when following the flow of traffic. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: gregmac
comments.why_zh: 设计速度与标示限速之别；这是评论者必看的视频
comments.quote_zh: 现在这个话题一出现，我想到的就是这个视频
comments.text_zh: 欧洲有更多设计速度更低的道路。弯道、窄车道、路边停车、紧邻道路的树木/杆子等等。这些东西会让人开得更慢，因为开快会让人觉得不安全。在北美，道路通常完全相反地建造，长长的直路和宽阔的车道，所以设计速度其实相当高——即使那并不是本意。人们开得快，是因为那个速度让人感觉安全，但其实并不安全，因为那里有行人和转弯。然后我们又用低限速来“修补”这种糟糕的道路设计。现在这个话题一出现，我想到的就是这个视频：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Europe has a lot more roads with a lower design speed. Curves, narrow lanes, on-street parking, trees/poles/etc close to the road. These things cause people to drive slower, because it doesn't feel safe to go fast. In North America, roads are usually built in the complete opposite way, with long straight roads and wide lanes, so the design speed is actually quite high -- even if that wasn't the intent. People go fast, because it feels safe to go that speed, but isn't, because there are pedestrians and turns. We then "fix" that shit road design by having low speed limits. This video is all I think of when this discussion comes up now: [VIDEO]

comments.author: xputer
comments.story_title: Car accidents cause death, injury and trauma. Why do we shrug them off?
comments.why_zh: 道路设计应让司机自然减速，而不是依赖标志
comments.quote_zh: 我们的道路设计应该把人为失误考虑进去。
comments.text_zh: 抱歉，但这真的错得离谱。美国的道路设计极度依赖个人责任。我们把路设计得像高速公路一样宽，然后在路边放个小牌子写着限速 35mph。我们需要的是少强调个人责任，承认人会犯错，毕竟我们都是人。我们的道路设计应该把人为失误考虑进去。道路设计本身应该让司机在危险区域附近自然地减速。例如看这个视频：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Sorry but this is just so wrong. American road design is super predicated on personal responsibility. We design roads that are as wide as freeways and then put a little sign on the side that says 35mph speed limit. What we need is less focus on personal responsibility and accept that people make mistakes, we're all human after all. Our roads should be designed with human error in mind. The road design itself should make it natural for drivers to slow down near dangerous areas. See this video for example: [VIDEO]

comments.author: xputer
comments.story_title: Car accidents cause death, injury and trauma. Why do we shrug them off?
comments.why_zh: 通过道路设计刻意让汽车在需要处减速
comments.quote_zh: 而是通过道路设计，在需要的地方刻意让汽车减速。
comments.text_zh: 并不是说要把道路本身变得更窄或更弯。而是通过道路设计，在需要的地方刻意让汽车减速。例如看这个视频：[VIDEO] 除此之外，美国的道路分类普遍做得很差。它们常常试图同时充当高吞吐量道路和服务目的地的街道。这种混合道路被称为“stroads”，对所有人都不好。Stroads 不利于让汽车快速通行，因为有很多冲突点（车道出入口、交叉口等）迫使司机不断减速。它们也不利于服务目的地，因为众多冲突点让 stroads 非常危险，尤其是当你不在车里时。例如看这个视频：[LINK]
comments.text: It's not about making the roads more narrow or winding per se. It's about deliberately slowing cars down where they need to, through the road design. See this video for example: [VIDEO] Besides that, roads in the US are generally poorly classified. They're often trying to both function as both high throughput roads and destination serving streets. Such hybrid roads are known as "stroads" and they're bad for everyone involved. Stroads are bad for moving cars fast due to the many conflict points (driveways, intersections, etc.) that force drivers to constantly slow down. They are also bad at serving destinations because the many conflict points make stroads very dangerous, especially if you're not in a car. See this video for example: [LINK]

comments.quote_zh: Not Just Bikes 有一个很棒的视频讲了这个
comments.text_zh: Not Just Bikes 有一个很棒的视频讲了这个：[VIDEO] 太长不看版：人们不会死盯着自己的速度表看，所以改限速基本不会影响人们的实际驾驶速度。要真正改变这一点，你得改道路设计。

comments.author: YawningAngel
comments.story_title: Even after $100B, self-driving cars are going nowhere
comments.why_zh: 司机依据的是道路设计给的暗示，而不是牌子上的限速
comments.text_zh: 不过限速其实不是这么起作用的。人们的判断来自道路设计和路况，而不是限速牌上写的是什么。仅仅在纸面上改限速是危险的，因为它会让你以为自己改变了交通行为，而实际上并没有。[VIDEO] 详细讲了这一点
comments.text: That's not really how speed limits work though. People take their cues from road design and conditions, not what the speed limit actually is. Virtually changing speed limits is dangerous because it causes you to think you are altering the behaviour of traffic without actually doing so. [VIDEO] goes into detail on this

comments.author: CalRobert
comments.story_title: Wales' 20mph speed limit: How has the first month gone?
comments.why_zh: 决定车速的是街道设计，而不是限速
comments.quote_zh: 如果你想让司机开到 20mph，你就得把街道设计成再快一点就让人觉得不舒服。
comments.text_zh: 尽管那些抱怨的司机留下的评论让人沮丧，但它揭示出这里的问题在于依赖限速而不是街道设计。如果你想让司机开到 20mph，你就得把街道设计成再快一点就让人觉得不舒服。[VIDEO] 讨论了这一点。另外我注意到，那些抱怨的司机大多没有提到：家里有个爱跑的小小孩、总是想挣脱你的手冲上马路，那是什么感觉。
comments.text: As much as the comments from complaining drivers are frustrating, it reveals that the problem here is relying on speed limits and not street design. If you want drivers to go 20mph, you need to design the street so going any faster feels uncomfortable. [VIDEO] discuses this. Also, I notice that most of those drivers complaining don't address what it's like to have a small child who's a runner and is always trying to get loose of your grip and run in to the street.

comments.author: TomK32
comments.story_title: Making an intersection unsafe for pedestrians to save seconds for drivers
comments.why_zh: 道路设计塑造驾驶行为的好坏
comments.quote_zh: 道路设计才是决定驾驶好坏的原因。
comments.text_zh: 道路设计才是决定驾驶好坏的原因。你描述的那条路应该在盲弯前收窄，这样司机（通常会在不知不觉中）就会在进弯前减速。至于人行横道，用分隔车道、给行人提供安全空间的小型安全岛会有帮助。[VIDEO]
comments.text: The road design is what causes bad or good driving. The road you describe should narrow before the blind curve so the drivers would (often enough unconsciously) slow down before it. For the pedestrian crossing, small islands that separate the lanes and give pedestrians a safe space will help. [VIDEO]

comments.author: xracy
comments.story_title: Speed traps have no long-term effect on speeding: study
comments.why_zh: 收窄车道比执法更能让车流慢下来
comments.quote_zh: 让交通慢下来的办法，是把车道收窄。
comments.text_zh: [VIDEO] 这感觉像是在一个本来就不太有效的办法上加倍下注。让交通慢下来的办法，是把车道收窄。你还可以加弯道、树木或挑檐来给道路投下阴影，这会打断道路的连续性，让人从远处更难判断路况。
comments.text: [VIDEO] This feels like doubling down on something that's not super effective. The way to make traffic slower, is to make road lanes narrower. You can also add curves/trees or overhangs to add shadows to the road, which breaks up the roadway and makes it harder to reason about from a distance.
